name: ChatPRD
claim: AI product-management platform that drafts and improves PRDs, one-pagers, user stories and tech specs from natural-language prompts.
spec_shape: PRD documents plus reusable custom templates; vendor claims one-pagers, user stories and technical specs. Exact section schema NOT published on the marketing site or llms.txt — template structure is user-definable rather than a fixed contract.
elicitation: Chat-first against a persona ('AI chief product officer'); also 'turn customer research and meeting notes into specifications' (doc/notes paste). No documented interview mode with forced clarifying questions.
testability: No documented acceptance-criteria generator or falsifiability mechanism; output is prose optimised for human reading. Third-party reviews specifically criticise the lack of AI-agent-consumable output.
limitations: Site is marketing-thin; PRD section schema unverified from primary source. Vendor claim of 100k+ PMs is unaudited. No customer-evidence ingestion layer (widely cited criticism).

name: ChatPRD MCP Server
claim: Authenticated MCP endpoint exposing product documents to AI coding tools as live context.
spec_shape: Tool surface (observed in llms.txt): list/retrieve/search/create/update documents, list projects and organizations, browse org documents, find chats, retrieve templates, read user profile.
elicitation: Not an elicitation surface — a retrieval/write surface. The spec is authored elsewhere and served to a coding agent over Streamable HTTP with OAuth bearer auth, RFC 9728 discovery, PKCE.
testability: None directly; it transports the spec rather than testing it. Notable: docs instruct agents to confirm before modifying documents/workspaces.
limitations: Access follows user permissions; requires auth so the tool schema could not be exercised. Value depends entirely on upstream spec quality.

name: BuildBetter
claim: Customer-intelligence platform that generates PRDs and scoping docs grounded in captured customer calls, tickets and Slack threads with citations.
spec_shape: Docs, PRDs, planning and scoping docs, roadmaps, changelogs, reports, dashboards, clusters. Distinctive layer: Signals — vendor claims 35+ signal types carrying sentiment, severity and business impact, plus customer-specific taxonomy.
elicitation: Meeting/call ingest (bot and bot-less local recorder, or import), Slack threads, support tickets, CSV, AI surveys, social listening, CRM enrichment, REST API. Spec is derived from captured evidence rather than typed intent — inverted elicitation.
testability: No acceptance criteria mechanism. Instead the falsifiability is evidential: claims in a report trace to source conversations. Vendor claims 99% evidence coverage vs 20-28% for keyword/vector/hybrid search (own benchmark, unaudited) and 98% classification accuracy.
limitations: All accuracy figures are vendor self-benchmarks against unnamed baselines. Exact quote/timestamp anchoring format in PRDs not documented on the page. Presupposes an existing customer-call corpus — useless at true cold start.

name: Figr
claim: PRD generator that refuses the blank prompt: ingests existing product context first, then structures a PRD grounded in what the product actually does.
spec_shape: PRD kept connected to user flows and prototypes on the same canvas — spec and design artifact co-located rather than a detached document.
elicitation: Context ingest before generation: live webapp, analytics, user interviews, competitor screenshots. Explicitly positioned against blank-prompt generation.
testability: Not documented. Grounding is in current-product reality rather than in testable criteria.
limitations: Characterised via a third-party roundup, not primary fetch — segment-competitor sources are vendor-published and self-favouring. Spec field schema unverified.

name: Keeborg
claim: Spec generator producing a multi-document stack formatted for AI-agent consumption with cross-document consistency checking.
spec_shape: Vendor claims a full 8-document spec stack with automatic cross-document consistency (the specific eight documents were not verified from primary source).
elicitation: Not verified.
testability: Not verified; consistency-checking is a coherence mechanism, not a falsifiability one.
limitations: Sourced from the vendor's own comparison blog — maximally self-favouring. The '8-document stack' is an unverified vendor claim and the count should not be quoted downstream without a primary read. Cross-document consistency is the interesting mechanism if real.

name: ContextArk
claim: Spec tool built for AI coding agents that emphasises non-goals and acceptance criteria to prevent scope creep in Cursor/Claude Code.
spec_shape: Reported to foreground non-goals (explicit out-of-scope) and acceptance criteria as first-class spec fields.
elicitation: Not verified.
testability: Acceptance criteria are a named primary feature — one of the few in this segment claiming it. Falsifiability format unverified.
limitations: Third-party mention only; no primary fetch. Small/unproven vendor. The non-goals + acceptance-criteria pairing is the transferable idea regardless of this specific product's survival.

name: IdeaPlan Forge
claim: AI document generation embedded in a broader PM operating system (feedback, roadmap, releases).
spec_shape: PRDs and PM documents inside a wider product-management suite.
elicitation: Not verified; presumed chat/template.
testability: Not documented.
limitations: Known only via IdeaPlan's own comparison pages, which rank IdeaPlan favourably. Spec mechanism appears to be a feature of a suite rather than the core product — weak differentiation for Actionist's purposes.

name: FreePRD.ai
claim: Free unlimited PRD generation with no signup, positioned explicitly as a ChatPRD alternative.
spec_shape: Template-driven PRD output; reported hundreds of templates.
elicitation: Prompt plus template selection.
testability: None documented; reviewers describe output as adequate first drafts lacking refinement.
limitations: Third-party sourced. A thin wrapper over a general LLM with template prompts; no persistent context, no evidence layer, no testability. Included for denominator completeness only.

name: FifthDraft
claim: Free unlimited PRD generator requiring no account; pick product type, describe feature, receive structured output.
spec_shape: Structured PRD output keyed off a product-type selection — the type acts as a schema selector.
elicitation: Two-field intake: product type (enum) then free-text feature description. Notable as the minimum viable elicitation in this segment.
testability: None documented.
limitations: Third-party sourced, not fetched. Extremely thin product; interesting only because the product-type-as-schema-selector pattern is cheap and reusable.

name: Taskade AI Software Development Proposal Generator
claim: Template-driven AI generator producing software development proposals inside a general workspace tool.
spec_shape: Proposal document sections; generic rather than dev-specific.
elicitation: Prompt into a fixed proposal template.
testability: None.
limitations: Generic AI generator that, per market analysis, knows nothing about sprints, tech stacks, APIs or dev milestones. Denominator entry.

name: Jama Connect
claim: Requirements/engineering management platform now repositioned as an 'Intelligent Engineering Management Platform' with spec-driven development for AI agents.
spec_shape: Items in a semantic product graph spanning disciplines. Vendor states scale of up to 10 million items per project and 100 million per instance. AI-generated requirements, test cases and traceability adhering to industry standards.
elicitation: Structured authoring against item types plus, as of this observation, MCP-shared context so engineers and AI agents work from the same product graph. Vendor explicitly frames the graph as improving LLM inference quality and token efficiency.
testability: Requirements link to test cases and verification; integrations with Xray, TestRail, LDRA, Parasoft. Compliance regimes named: ISO 26262, DO-178C, ISO 13485, FDA 21 CFR Part 11, ASPICE. AI governance with approvals and audit trails.
limitations: Marketing page did not define Live Traceability, did not disclose the item schema, and did not mention Advisor. Item-count figures are vendor claims. The 2026 repositioning toward spec-driven/MCP is directionally the most Actionist-relevant signal in this segment but is a vendor narrative, not observed behaviour.

name: Jama Connect Advisor
claim: NLP requirements-authoring assistant that checks the quality of individual requirement statements against INCOSE best practice and EARS syntax.
spec_shape: Operates at single-statement granularity ('single statement authoring'), not document granularity — the unit of quality is one requirement sentence.
elicitation: Author writes a requirement; the tool critiques and reshapes it toward a constrained grammar. Elicitation-by-correction rather than elicitation-by-interview.
testability: This is the core mechanism: EARS-shaped requirements resemble test cases directly, so quality checking and testability are the same operation.
limitations: The fetched page is an announcement — it does NOT enumerate which INCOSE rules or EARS patterns are implemented, and describes no scoring or flagging mechanism. Claims about detecting ambiguity/passive voice/vagueness could NOT be confirmed and must not be repeated as observed. Underlying grammar (see com-b-013) is verified; this product's implementation of it is not.

name: EARS notation (Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax)
claim: A constrained-natural-language grammar for requirements; not a product but the mechanism several commercial tools implement.
spec_shape: Ruleset: zero-or-many preconditions, zero-or-one trigger, one system name, one-or-many system responses, clauses always in the same temporal order. Six patterns — Ubiquitous 'The <system> shall <response>'; State-driven 'WHILE <precondition>, the <system> shall <response>'; Event-driven 'WHEN <trigger>, the <system> shall <response>'; Optional-feature 'WHERE <feature included>, the <system> shall <response>'; Unwanted-behaviour 'IF <condition>, THEN the <system> shall <response>'; Complex, combining keywords.
elicitation: Structural coercion. Because trigger, precondition, system name and response are structurally mandatory, an author cannot complete the sentence without noticing missing information — the article's phrasing is that EARS exposes what must be discovered rather than hiding it in vague prose.
testability: Highest in the entire survey. EARS statements resemble test cases by construction; fixed clause order maps to given/when/then. Quoted senior engineer position: if you cannot write it in EARS, you do not understand it.
limitations: Origin verified: developed 2009 at Rolls-Royce Aero Engines during analysis of an airworthiness regulation for an aero engine control system, published at IEEE RE09. Adopter list (Bosch, Daimler, Dyson, Honeywell, Intel, NASA, Siemens) is a vendor-page claim. Note the page is Jama-published, so its framing favours Jama tooling. Some template text was placeholder-stripped in the fetched render; patterns above reflect the standard published EARS structure and should be re-checked against Mavin's original RE09 paper before client quotation.

name: IBM Engineering Requirements Management DOORS Next
claim: Enterprise requirements management for regulated, long-lifecycle engineering with formal baselines and multi-level traceability.
spec_shape: Artifacts as the atomic unit, organised into Modules (hierarchical specification documents). Every module artifact also persists as a base artifact in the module folder or Base Artifacts folder. Configurable data model, folders, attributes, views, filters, tags, glossary terms.
elicitation: Structured authoring into a predefined data model, plus round-trip import/export. Not conversational — the schema is designed up front by an administrator and authors fill it.
testability: System-defined link types include Validated By (Validates/Validated By), which captures the relationship between a requirement and a Quality Management object such as a test case. Also Artifact Term Reference (Affects/Affected By), Embeds, and generic Link. Custom link types configurable via Manage Project Properties.
limitations: Primary IBM product page returned HTTP 403; schema detail above is reconstructed from IBM docs plus SodiusWillert and Softacus third-party guides. Baselines are component/project-level (unlike DOORS Classic), and cross-component traceability requires a Global Configuration context — a real structural constraint. No AI/watsonx requirements feature confirmed.

name: DOORS Next suspect-link change propagation
claim: Change-impact mechanism: editing a requirement automatically marks associated links as suspect.
spec_shape: Link state carries a suspicion flag; impact surfaces as a work queue of suspect links rather than as a diff.
elicitation: Not elicitation — post-hoc integrity maintenance. Relevant because it answers 'what happens to the spec when reality moves', which most AI-PRD tools in this survey simply do not answer.
testability: Enables impact and cost assessment of proposed changes and alerts contributing teams to potential impacts on linked artifacts.
limitations: Third-party vendor blog (Softacus is a consultancy). Mechanism is well-attested across multiple independent sources in this sweep.

name: IBM Engineering Requirements Management DOORS (Classic)
claim: The long-lived predecessor RM tool, still entrenched where organisations have long product lifecycles and historical investment.
spec_shape: Formal modules, objects, attributes, baselines. Project-level rather than component-level baselining (contrast with DOORS Next).
elicitation: Structured authoring; DXL scripting for automation.
testability: Traceability matrices to verification artifacts.
limitations: Not fetched. Included for denominator completeness — architecturally superseded by DOORS Next for new work, so its interest to Actionist is historical.

name: Siemens Polarion ALM
claim: Full integration of requirements, change and test management in one ALM platform.
spec_shape: Work-item-based model unifying requirements, changes and tests in a single item type system with configurable workflows.
elicitation: Structured authoring into work items; document-oriented LiveDocs.
testability: Test management is native to the same item model rather than integrated across a boundary — requirements and their verification share one schema.
limitations: Not fetched. Reported steep learning curve and complex implementation for companies without Siemens infrastructure. Gravity comes from Siemens PLM adjacency more than from spec mechanism quality.

name: PTC Codebeamer
claim: Highly configurable ALM for complex regulated product organisations covering requirements, risks and verification.
spec_shape: Configurable trackers/item types able to represent industry-specific requirement shapes; workflows, risks and verification activities in one model.
elicitation: Structured authoring with heavy per-industry configuration.
testability: Verification activities modelled alongside requirements; PTC reports extending AI investment into requirements and test management.
limitations: Not fetched. Configurability is the selling point and the cost — the schema is a project, not a default.

name: Visure Requirements ALM
claim: Requirements ALM for safety-critical and highly regulated industries with bidirectional traceability across thousands of interconnected items.
spec_shape: Requirement items with bidirectional trace links; out-of-the-box compliance templates for ISO 26262, IEC 62304, DO-178C.
elicitation: Structured authoring against standard-specific templates — the regulation supplies the schema.
testability: Traceability is designed to produce compliance evidence, so the spec's job is to prove itself to an auditor.
limitations: Not fetched; Visure also publishes its own comparison content, so rankings citing it are self-interested. Acknowledged drawback: oversized with high implementation effort for less regulated projects.

name: Modern Requirements4DevOps
claim: Requirements and traceability layer built directly inside Microsoft Azure DevOps rather than as a separate platform.
spec_shape: Extends Azure DevOps work items with requirements structures, documents, baselines and trace matrices.
elicitation: Authoring inside existing ADO work items; template-driven document assembly (Smart Docs).
testability: Trace matrices link requirements to ADO test cases — reuses the host tool's test model.
limitations: Not fetched. Architecturally interesting for Actionist as the 'ride the host schema' strategy: no new object model, only added structure and traceability over an existing one.

name: ReqSuite RM
claim: Requirements management aimed at medium-sized product developers, positioned as lighter-weight than DOORS/Polarion class tools.
spec_shape: Requirements with configurable templates and quality guidance.
elicitation: Template- and guidance-driven authoring with automated quality assistance.
testability: Not verified.
limitations: Known only through ReqSuite's own comparison blog and a G2 alternatives listing — self-favouring sources. Included because the mid-market position is closer to Actionist's likely users than the aerospace-grade tools.

name: Lovable
claim: Prompt-to-app builder generating frontend, backend, database, auth and integrations from natural-language description in a per-project chat.
spec_shape: No PRD artifact. Documented workflow is describe, review and iterate, publish, optionally sync to GitHub/GitLab. Each project holds its chat, preview, code and version history — the chat transcript is the de facto spec.
elicitation: Conversational iteration rather than upfront interrogation. Third-party field tests report Lovable becomes technical quickly and that users spend time correcting assumptions and clarifying requirements after generation rather than before it.
testability: None documented at the spec layer.
limitations: Docs index page did not document a distinct chat vs build/agent mode, clarifying-question behaviour, or any plan artifact — absence here is absence of documentation, not proof of absence in product. Lovable also publishes competitor comparisons, so its own guides are self-favouring.

name: Lovable Knowledge (project & workspace context)
claim: Persistent plain-text instruction store the agent consults on every message — the closest thing in the builder segment to a durable spec.
spec_shape: Two levels, each a plain-text field capped at 10,000 characters. Workspace knowledge: coding style, naming conventions, preferred libraries, architecture patterns, testing rules, brand voice, things to avoid; owner/admin-managed. Project knowledge, with documented example headings: Project overview, Users, Key database tables, Design guidelines, Architecture rules, Domain terminology. Docs explicitly note there is no formal PRD template.
elicitation: Hand-authored, not elicited. Docs advise writing it like onboarding documentation and being specific — the cited example contrasts 'Always enable TypeScript strict mode. Never use any.' against vague guidance.
testability: None. Knowledge is directive, not falsifiable — it states what should be true rather than what must be demonstrated.
limitations: Two honest limits documented by the vendor: the 10,000-character cap per field, and that in very long conversations with a lot of context instructions may not always be followed consistently. Precedence rule is soft — project knowledge 'generally' wins over workspace on conflict. Knowledge is always-on background context, unlike skills which load on demand; it competes with project code, connector knowledge and AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md for attention.

name: Replit Agent (Plan mode)
claim: Prompt-to-app agent with an explicit pre-build planning mode gated by user approval.
spec_shape: An ordered task list produced before any code or data is modified — decomposition, not description. Plan mode also explores different approaches and weighs trade-offs.
elicitation: Plan mode activated by clicking Plan in the chat input or by asking the agent in natural language. Docs describe the agent as taking ideas, helping refine them, then making them real. Independent field testing found Replit Agent asked clarifying questions before starting — which database, whether authentication was needed, what happens when a reminder date passes — and the reviewer concluded it was the only tool tested that treated a vague description as vague.
testability: No acceptance criteria, but two real gates: an explicit Accept tasks / Revise plan dialog before building, and checkpoints allowing rollback to any previous state. Agent also self-tests its work.
limitations: The clarifying-question behaviour is a third-party observation of one session, not a documented guarantee — the official docs do not promise proactive interrogation. Design Canvas mockups precede code but are visual, not specified. Paid actions require separate 'Allow once' confirmation, conflating scope approval with billing approval.

name: Bolt.new
claim: In-browser prompt-to-full-stack-app builder offering an explicit choice between planning first and generating immediately.
spec_shape: Project type chosen at intake as an enum — Website, Slides, App, or Prototype — which conditions generation. No documented spec document.
elicitation: Chat-style prompt box with a Plan option and a Build now option side by side, so the user elects the depth of specification. Alternative intakes: import from Figma or GitHub, or fork a template.
testability: None at the spec layer; instead Bolt automatically tests, refactors and iterates to reduce errors — verification is delegated to the agent, not exposed as criteria.
limitations: The landing page confirms Plan vs Build-now exists but does NOT describe what planning involves or whether it asks clarifying questions — the mechanism is unverified. Model routing is automatic across Standard and Max agent tiers, so behaviour is not stable across runs. Independent test reported a working app in about three minutes without interrogation.

name: v0 by Vercel
claim: Prompt-to-UI generator focused on frontend components and pages.
spec_shape: No spec artifact; the generated interface is the specification.
elicitation: Single prompt to immediate generation. Independent field testing describes building a gorgeous interface in about two minutes with no database behind it and no way to save anything.
testability: None.
limitations: Not fetched. Deliberately scoped to frontend — no backend generation, so requirements about data, state and persistence are structurally out of scope rather than merely unasked. The clearest example in this survey of generation speed traded against specification depth.

name: Base44
claim: Consumer-feeling AI app builder that turns a prompt into a structured project with screens, data models, authentication and core workflows.
spec_shape: Reported to materialise the prompt as a structured project comprising screens, data models, authentication and core workflows — an implicit schema, presented as a working product almost immediately rather than as a document.
elicitation: Sign up, choose a template, customise immediately, with a guided tour. Reported to push the user to describe the app, then convert that prompt into the structured project. Characterised as assuming users want to dive in and learn by doing, abstracting away many decisions.
testability: None documented.
limitations: Primary fetch was not completed (tool limit reached); all detail is from third-party comparisons, several published by direct competitors (Lovable, Softr, monday.com) and therefore self-favouring. The screens/data-models/auth/workflows decomposition is the useful signal and should be re-verified from Base44's own docs before client use.

name: Replit Design Canvas / Design Mode
claim: Visual mockup surface for exploring designs before committing to code.
spec_shape: Mockups plus a hands-on visual editor; Design is also a selectable project type.
elicitation: Prototype-as-question — the mockup is shown so the user can react to it, substituting recognition for articulation.
testability: None; visual agreement is not falsifiable.
limitations: Documented as part of the Agent page rather than independently specified. Directly relevant to Actionist's 'when to prototype vs when to ask' question: Replit's answer is prototype for look-and-feel, ask for data and behaviour.

name: Softr
claim: No-code app builder over existing data sources (Airtable, Google Sheets, databases) with block-based page composition.
spec_shape: Data source plus block/template selection — the connected data schema IS the spec, so requirements elicitation is largely replaced by pointing at existing structured data.
elicitation: Connect data, choose template, compose blocks. Minimal natural-language elicitation.
testability: None.
limitations: Not fetched; Softr publishes competitor comparisons and is thus self-interested as a source. Included because data-source-first intake is a genuinely different answer to the elicitation problem — it sidesteps intent capture entirely when the data already exists.

name: Glide
claim: Builds business apps from spreadsheet or database data with AI-assisted layout.
spec_shape: Table schema drives screens and roles; app structure derived from data shape.
elicitation: Data-first, same family as Softr — the spreadsheet is the requirements document.
testability: None.
limitations: Not fetched. Denominator entry for the data-first intake pattern.

name: Bubble
claim: Visual full-stack no-code development platform with explicit data types and workflow logic.
spec_shape: Explicit and unusually legible object model: Data types with fields, plus Workflows as When-event-Then-actions chains. The workflow grammar is structurally close to event-driven EARS and to Gherkin.
elicitation: Manual construction by the builder; AI assistance layered on later. Requirements are expressed by building them.
testability: Workflow conditions are inspectable and enumerable, so behaviour can be read off the model — better than any pure-chat builder here, though not test-generating.
limitations: Not fetched. Long learning curve. Relevant to Actionist mainly as evidence that a When/Then workflow grammar is learnable by non-engineers at scale — a decade-long natural experiment supporting the EARS-style approach.

name: Mocha
claim: AI app builder positioned against Lovable/Bolt/v0 for non-technical builders.
spec_shape: Not verified.
elicitation: Prompt-driven; not verified.
testability: Not documented.
limitations: Known only via its own comparison blog — maximally self-favouring source. Thin evidence; denominator entry only.

name: Magic Patterns
claim: AI prototyping tool for product teams generating UI from prompts.
spec_shape: UI artifacts; no spec document.
elicitation: Prompt to prototype.
testability: None.
limitations: Not fetched; appears in a third-party prototyping-stack comparison. Prototype-as-spec pattern, same limitation class as v0.

name: Cursor
claim: AI code editor whose spec surface is rules files consumed before editing.
spec_shape: Project rules files (.cursorrules / .cursor/rules) — persistent directives, structurally the same idea as Lovable Knowledge and AGENTS.md.
elicitation: Hand-authored rules plus in-editor chat. No elicitation mechanism.
testability: None at spec layer.
limitations: Not fetched. Included because rules-file-as-spec is now a de facto cross-product convention (Lovable docs explicitly read AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md), which matters for what format Actionist's ProductSpec should be emittable in.

name: Proposify
claim: Proposal platform whose AI drafts editable executive summaries, cover letters, scopes of work and project approaches from pasted discovery material.
spec_shape: Content Library of approved reusable content — product/service descriptions, pricing, case studies, images — plus a separate Pricing/Fee Library holding current pricing. Templates carry custom fields and variables; interactive quotes let buyers adjust quantities and add-ons.
elicitation: Third-party reporting describes ingesting pasted call notes, meeting transcripts and project requirements to draft from a single prompt — discovery notes in, draft SOW out.
testability: No acceptance criteria. The governance analogue: admins set conditions triggering manager approval based on deal size and discount size; roles and permissions restrict editing, sending and asset access; templates lock pre-written clauses while allowing per-deal customisation.
limitations: Important gap — the fetched product page did NOT describe the AI mechanism, transcript ingestion, or any dedicated scope-of-work structure; those claims come from a third-party guide and remain unverified. The same guide flags the real problem as governance: verifying that AI-generated documents match what was actually scoped, priced and agreed before reaching a client. Approval workflows are gated to higher tiers.

name: PandaDoc
claim: Document automation platform covering SOW, MSA and proposal generation through to signature and payment.
spec_shape: Template-based documents with variables; reported 750+ templates. Scope is prose within a template, not a structured object.
elicitation: Template selection plus CRM field merge; no requirements interrogation.
testability: None. E-signature is the commitment mechanism — agreement replaces verification.
limitations: Not fetched. Reported pricing from $35/user/month (Essentials) is a third-party figure. Generic document tooling with no software-scoping semantics.

name: Qwilr
claim: Proposal tool that outputs an interactive web page rather than a PDF or traditional document.
spec_shape: Web-page proposal with interactive pricing/quote blocks.
elicitation: Template composition.
testability: None; buyer interaction with pricing is measurable but scope is not falsifiable.
limitations: Not fetched. The page-not-PDF choice is the only differentiator relevant here — it makes the scope artifact live and updatable rather than a frozen attachment.

name: FlowEdge
claim: AI proposal/SOW/contract generator aimed at independent consultants, fractional executives and small agencies.
spec_shape: Reported to produce structured sections including deliverables, payment terms and acceptance criteria — one of the few in the scoping segment where acceptance criteria are named as an output section.
elicitation: Reads the consultant's stored profile and service descriptions, plus uploaded meeting notes or intake forms. Profile memory means client-specific variation is handled without re-templating.
testability: Acceptance criteria appear as a document section — contractual rather than executable, but present, which most peers lack.
limitations: Not fetched; all detail including pricing (reported pay-as-you-go from $1/document, plans from $18/month Solo, $48/month Business) comes from FlowEdge's own comparison content, in which FlowEdge is ranked as producing the most complete output. Treat the ranking as advertising and the acceptance-criteria section as the only durable observation.

name: Loopio
claim: Enterprise RFP response platform with content library and AI-assisted question matching.
spec_shape: Question-answer pairs in a governed content library; the RFP supplies the question schema.
elicitation: Inverted — the buyer's RFP questionnaire performs the elicitation and the vendor's job is retrieval and assembly. Structurally the cleanest 'someone else wrote the spec questions' model in the survey.
testability: Team approval workflows gate answer accuracy; no executable criteria.
limitations: Not fetched. Explicitly flagged in market analysis as too expensive and complex for a 5-person agency. Interesting as a mechanism, wrong scale for Actionist's users.

name: Responsive (formerly RFPIO)
claim: Enterprise RFP and response management with content library and AI question matching.
spec_shape: Governed answer library keyed to recurring procurement questions.
elicitation: Buyer-questionnaire-driven, same inversion as Loopio.
testability: Approval workflows only.
limitations: Not fetched. Enterprise procurement scale; duplicate mechanism to com-b-039. Denominator entry.

name: Forecast
claim: Professional-services platform with project scoping and estimation — phases, tasks, assignment, deadlines and placeholder-based pipeline scoping.
spec_shape: Phases containing tasks with assignees and deadlines; placeholders and tentative bookings for unwon work; demand forecast weighted by win probability.
elicitation: Manual decomposition by a delivery lead. No intent capture.
testability: None — estimates are predictions, not criteria.
limitations: Not fetched. This is resource planning wearing scoping vocabulary; the probability-weighted pipeline is the one idea worth noting (representing scope confidence as a number attached to unwon work).

name: KuberAgent SOW & Project Proposal Generator
claim: Free SOW and project proposal generator.
spec_shape: Standard SOW sections.
elicitation: Form/prompt to template.
testability: None.
limitations: Not fetched. Free lead-generation utility. Denominator entry; no mechanism of interest.

name: Galorath SEER
claim: Parametric software cost and effort estimation using sizing models.
spec_shape: Size drivers (function points, SLOC, complexity) mapped to effort, cost and schedule estimates with ranges.
elicitation: Analyst supplies size and complexity parameters; the model supplies the estimate. Requires a scope that already exists.
testability: Estimates carry ranges and confidence levels — a genuinely quantified uncertainty representation, rare in this survey.
limitations: Not fetched. Sits downstream of specification: consumes scope rather than eliciting it. Included because parametric confidence ranges are the strongest prior art for representing estimate uncertainty numerically.

name: Cucumber Studio
claim: BDD collaboration platform positioning itself as the single source of truth where whole teams manage executable specifications together.
spec_shape: Gherkin feature files with scenarios and acceptance criteria, rendered as readable living documentation. Business and technology sides jointly author acceptance criteria.
elicitation: Three-phase team-centric cycle: define your idea (collaboratively write specifications/acceptance criteria), test your code (automate scenarios), learn in production. The platform lets non-technical participants read and refine executable specifications without needing technical tools.
testability: Strongest in the survey alongside EARS. Specifications ARE the tests: living documentation is verified with every developer check-in via Git integration, so documentation staleness is structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged. Results surface through analytics dashboards for stakeholder visibility.
limitations: Fetched page is marketing; no schema, pricing or automation detail. Product ownership moved from Cucumber/HipTest branding to SmartBear (cucumber.io URL 301s to smartbear.com), so long-term positioning is uncertain. Real-world caveat from the segment sweep: BDD's value depends on cross-functional participation — without stakeholders it is overhead for nothing.

name: Xray (BDD in Jira)
claim: Jira-native test management storing Gherkin scenarios as Jira issues linked to requirement issues for coverage.
spec_shape: Cucumber Test issue type holding Scenario or Scenario Outline; Pre-Condition issue type holding Gherkin Backgrounds and reusable setup. Feature-level content is deliberately not imported because the feature should already exist as a Jira requirement issue such as a story.
elicitation: Not elicitation — binding. A tag carrying a requirement key causes a Tests link to be created between the Test and the requirement issue; a Cucumber Test created from a story is automatically linked to it.
testability: The sharpest coverage semantics found: a requirement issue displays as UNCOVERED when no test covers it. Traceability reports link requirements, tests, executions and defects. Bulk import/update from .feature files via REST API and CI plugins; export of .feature files from Tests and Pre-Conditions. Validates with Cucumber (multiple languages), Behave and SpecFlow.
limitations: Cloud doc page returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch; detail reconstructed from Xray's own indexed documentation plus third-party guides. The docs themselves surface the key unresolved tension: teams must choose where scenarios are mastered, since you preferably want only a single source of truth — Jira or the repo, not both. Backgrounds without a name produce derived Pre-Condition summaries listing test keys, which is a legibility cost.

name: Zephyr (Gherkin support)
claim: Jira-based test management offering one home for manual, automated and BDD testing.
spec_shape: Test cases including Gherkin-authored ones alongside manual and automated tests.
elicitation: Authoring within Jira test cases.
testability: Executable Gherkin plus consolidated reporting across test styles.
limitations: Not fetched. Positioned in third-party comparison as the choice for a single Jira-based home rather than for BDD depth specifically; weaker BDD semantics than Xray's coverage model.

name: Tricentis qTest
claim: Enterprise test management with BDD support, positioned for governance.
spec_shape: Test cases and requirements with enterprise traceability and audit trails.
elicitation: Structured authoring.
testability: Traceability and audit-grade reporting.
limitations: Not fetched. Same vendor discontinued SpecFlow, which is a material signal about commitment to the BDD tooling line. Governance-first rather than elicitation-first.

name: Reqnroll
claim: Open-source Cucumber-style BDD framework for .NET; the community successor to the discontinued SpecFlow, led by SpecFlow's original creator.
spec_shape: Gherkin feature files with full support including tagged Rule blocks; step definitions via regex or Cucumber expressions.
elicitation: None — consumes specifications written elsewhere. The name itself (Req + roll) signals requirements-first intent.
testability: Total: the feature file is the executable test. Runs on common operating systems and .NET versions including .NET 8.0, installed via NuGet.
limitations: Not fetched. Open source, maintained and sponsored by the community and companies that benefit — a sustainability model worth noting rather than assuming. Migration from SpecFlow described as deliberately near-drop-in. Included because SpecFlow's commercial discontinuation and this community reboot is the load-bearing fact about commercial BDD tooling risk in 2026.

name: SpecFlow + LivingDoc
claim: Formerly the most widely used .NET BDD framework with living documentation generation; discontinued by Tricentis.
spec_shape: Gherkin feature files rendered into browsable living documentation.
elicitation: None; consumes written specs.
testability: Executable feature files with generated documentation.
limitations: Not fetched. DISCONTINUED — this is the entry's main value. A widely adopted commercial-backed spec tool was withdrawn, stranding users until a community fork appeared. Directly relevant to how Actionist should think about spec-format lock-in: prefer a format that survives its tooling.

name: ContextQA
claim: AI-native test platform generating and self-healing tests from plain-English behaviour descriptions without a glue-code layer.
spec_shape: Plain-English behaviour statements compiled directly to executable tests — removes the step-definition layer that BDD frameworks require.
elicitation: Natural-language behaviour description; the notable claim is that no Gherkin discipline or step-definition authoring is required.
testability: High in principle: business-readable statements become runnable and self-heal against UI drift.
limitations: Ranked first in its own blog's top-10 BDD list — a self-published ranking and therefore advertising. Self-healing tests trade determinism for durability, which is a real correctness concern for acceptance criteria specifically: a test that heals itself may stop testing the original assertion. Not fetched.

name: Cucumber (open-source core)
claim: The de facto reference BDD implementation and the origin of the Gherkin Given/When/Then grammar.
spec_shape: Gherkin: Feature, Rule, Background, Scenario, Scenario Outline with Examples, and Given/When/Then/And/But steps. Feature files are framework-agnostic; step definitions must be rewritten per language.
elicitation: The three practices it encodes are discovery, formulation and automation — formulation is the step where an agreed example becomes a written scenario, which is precisely the elicitation-to-spec transition Actionist needs.
testability: Definitional. A scenario is simultaneously the requirement and its test.
limitations: Not fetched in this sweep (cucumber.io/tools/cucumberstudio 301'd to SmartBear, confirming the domain is live). Well-known caveats surfaced in the sweep: BDD scenarios run roughly 10-100x slower than unit tests and suit acceptance rather than design; the collaboration payoff requires stakeholder participation. Included as the grammar every commercial entry in this segment depends on.
